symptoms: You will see leaves being eaten away in the early stages.
The larva often keeps its head inside the pod while its body hangs outside.
You will see round holes on the pods.
The buds, flowers, and pods may have bore holes.
Infested flowers and pods are often webbed together.
prevention: Install pheromone traps to monitor the pest population.
Place traps at a rate of 4 to 5 per acre.
Keep traps at least 75 feet apart from each other.
Set traps one foot above the plant canopy.
practices: Check your fields weekly for the number of moths in your traps.
Remove and destroy any moths caught in the traps after you count them.
Look for natural predators like ladybird beetles in the field.
Avoid using insecticides if you see natural predators active in the crop.
